messages:
maria: quick heads-up — long-run soak on 68k ctx found steady KV memory growth even when we think prefixes should be reused. attaching heap profile in the thread (see perf job). main suspect: per-request nonce leaking into KV key format so reuse is poor.

ryan: can you paste an example of the key pattern you saw? my immediate hunch is we accidentally include a timestamp or request_id.

maria: sample from profiler trace (sanitized):
`kv_key="m:13|sess:U-12345|req:Q-20260201-87321|block:7"`

kevin: yep, `req:` is the problem — that gives every request a distinct namespace. that explains low hit-rate and linear mem growth per session. :facepalm:

maria: proposal: switch to session-scoped prefix keys + per-session block indexing, and add a TTL/last_access field to allow LRU-style eviction across sessions. rough sketch:

maria: ```
# keep model ver + session affinity, drop request id from key
kv_key = f"mv:{model_ver}|sess:{session_id}|lead:{lead_hash}|blk:{block_idx}"
metadata = {"last_access": now(), "origin": "prefix-cache"}
```

ryan: +1. also recommend sticky routing (session -> same node/GPU) where possible so the local KV store has higher locality. that reduces cross-node misses. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/rv1-kv-keying-fix -> staging (build 20260201.9)

kevin: couple of caveats: 1) sessions that are long-lived but mostly idle could still accumulate prefixes — we need a per-session cap (e.g., 256 blocks) and an eviction policy that demotes cold prefixes. 2) coarse keys increase fragmentation if we mix very different lead_hash granularities.

maria: agree. thoughts on eviction policy: track last_access_ts on prefix metadata, global LRU across prefixes, with a soft per-session cap and a hard global cap to avoid OOM. also an admission control to reject storing tiny single-block prefixes.

ryan: another nuance: batching heuristics — when multiple sessions are batched together, we must ensure block indices and KV pointers are distinct; otherwise coalescing could overwrite pointers if we rely on positional writebacks. add session_id to the per-batch slot mapping.

kevin: and kernel selection: some kernels expect contiguous KV memory layout; frequent evictions + re-inserts can cause fragmentation in the allocator and hurt throughput. might be worth testing a compacting eviction pass during low load windows.

maria: plan:
- open RFC/PR that updates key schema (drop request nonce, include model_ver+session+lead_hash)
- add per-prefix metadata (last_access, size, origin)
- implement per-session soft cap + global hard cap + LRU eviction
- add sticky routing opt and batch slot isolation checks
- run microbenchmarks: current vs session-prefix vs session-prefix+ttl (measure mem, hit-rate, p95 latency)

ryan: I can add the sticky-routing simulation and batch-isolation tests.

kevin: I'll prototype the per-prefix metadata and the LRU compaction job. also will instrument allocator fragmentation counters.

maria: cool — I'll draft the PR and perf job definitions tonight, will ping for reviews. tagging @kevin @ryan.

ryan: ack

kevin: ack

maria: thanks — goal is overnight perf runs and canary early tomorrow. :rocket:
